conviction_note: Quarter is pre-released (rev $56.8m, GM 26%), so the print turns on three things the 6-K and call must answer tonight: whether MGO-reviewed Q3 financials actually land on the Nov 16 deadline after BDO called the GHR deconsolidation an unresolved reportable event, how management addresses liquidity (cash $39.7m vs ~$39m remaining project spend, $15m minimum-liquidity covenant, FCCR test resuming Dec 31 after a 2025 breach, ATM switched off at $1.17), and Q4/2027 pricing; on balance a mild negative lean (p_up 45) on a stock with 144% realised vol that has sold every catalyst since September, so abs_move is large (18) and the signed number small.
bar: Revenue: company pre-release $56.8m (Oct 19 6-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000110465926118806/tm2628296d1_ex99-1.htm) against stale pre-release consensus that disagrees across sources: ~$54.4m and EPS $0.01 (Chartmill, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/GLAS/estimates), $52.3m / $0.01 (Benzinga, https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/GLAS/earnings-forecasts), $55.66m / $0.02 (FXEmpire, https://www.fxempire.com/stocks/glas/earnings). The bar is disputed, so every finding that rests on it is capped small; +4% is revenue vs the ~$54.4m midpoint and is already public. No company guidance for Q3 EPS. The live bar is really Q4 / 2027 commentary and the liquidity/accounting answers, for which there is no sourced consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest small: ~434k shares, 0.5% of float, 0.25 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement (Chartmill via search snippet, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/GLAS/ownership/short-interest); StockTitan shows ~652k shares, 0.8% of float, 1.0 days to cover, +50% vs prior period (https://www.stocktitan.net/overview/GLAS/, read 2026-11-16). Borrow fee ~0.3% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/glas/, snippet). Not a crowded short; no squeeze mechanism. Options: chain unusable (no two-sided ATM quotes), no skew number; open interest 12,854 with put/call OI 0.29, i.e. call-heavy, retail-tilted holder base. Tape: spot $1.18, -38.5% 5d, -52% 20d, -91% from 52w high, at 52w low, realised vol 144% annualised; from ~$8 on Sep 22 to $1.17 on Nov 16 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/glas/history/). Mid-November is tax-loss-selling season for a stock down ~85% since its Q3 ATM sales at $8.11.

findings.finding: The Q3 financials due tonight are the first test of an open auditor dispute: on Nov 6 the company had BDO resign at its request and re-appointed MGO (which it had itself removed on Sep 11) because BDO might not finish the Q3 review by the Nov 16 deadline; BDO had 'not completed its evaluation of the accounting for the deconsolidation transaction' (Glass House Retail, deconsolidated June 12, recorded as a $2.5m loss and a $13.8m Level-3 retained equity-method stake) and called it an 'unresolved issue and therefore a reportable event', which the board disputes; MGO had reviewed the same accounting in Q2 and found no material modification needed. The stock fell 33.2% on the Nov 12 disclosure. If MGO-reviewed interim statements are filed on time tonight, the filing-delay/cease-trade tail is removed; if not, or if the deconsolidation numbers move, it is a large negative.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The auditor-change disclosure itself (6-K filed Nov 12) moved the stock -33.16% on 9.4m shares vs a 1.4m median (baseline history, stockanalysis daily table). No prior instance of a filing delay for this issuer.
findings.why_not_priced: The -33% day priced the risk that the accounting dispute derails the filing; it cannot have priced the outcome, which is only visible when the 6-K with interim statements and MD&A hits EDGAR/SEDAR+ tonight. If the market believed on-time filing were certain the Nov 12 loss would have retraced on Nov 13-16; instead the stock went 1.25 -> 1.27 -> 1.17.
findings.independence: Same filing package: BDO's letter agreeing with the notice (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000110465926125544/tm2629652d1_ex99-2.htm) and the company's Nov 11 release stating the change was made over concern BDO could not finish the Q3 review by Nov 16 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000110465926125544/tm2629652d1_ex99-4.htm). The Nov 10 call announcement (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/glass-house-brands-host-third-210500984.html) predates the auditor change and still holds the Nov 16 date. Also context: CFO retiring (announced Sep 29) and a director resigned without stated reason (Oct 19 prelim release).

findings.finding: Liquidity and covenant arithmetic the Q3 MD&A must address: cash/restricted cash $39.7m at Sep 30 against 'roughly $39M remains to finish improvement projects and reach cash-flow positive' (Oct 19 release), a credit-facility covenant to keep liquidity above $15m 'at all times', ATM turned off (stock now $1.17 vs ATM average $8.41), $17.9m of scheduled principal in 2027, and the fixed-charge coverage test (1.25x TTM, breached at Dec 31 2025 and waived) resuming for the quarter ending Dec 31 2026 with TTM adjusted EBITDA dragged by Q1's -$4.2m and Q2's $5.7m. The spend is for a corroborated ramp (record 317k lbs, Greenhouse 2 fully planted), but the funding gap plus covenant pressure points to a waiver, new financing, deferred capex or going-concern language in tonight's documents.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing/funding headlines have coincided with selling: Kalkine headlined 'funding concerns' in the sell-off; the stock rose +9.35% on Oct 27 after the 6-K saying the ATM was turned off (baseline history, stockanalysis table), the one positive reaction to a company filing since September.
findings.why_not_priced: The covenant terms and the capex figure sit in two different documents (Q2 MD&A and Oct 19 release) and no wire summary of the prelim mentions debt or covenants (the Oct 19 release 'does not mention debt or borrowings'). If priced as a known funding gap there would be a disclosed waiver or financing already; instead management says it is 'sufficiently capitalized', so tonight's MD&A is the first place the reconciliation must appear. Partly priced: the equity is down ~85% since the ATM and trades near distressed levels relative to $71m debt plus $92.5m preferred.
findings.independence: Cash and capex figures: Oct 19 prelim release (https://finviz.com/news/403857/glass-house-brands-reports-preliminary-unaudited-third-quarter-financial-results-and-resignation-of-john-nichols-jr-from-board-of-directors). Debt schedule and covenants: Q2 interim statements (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000184873126000031/glas-20260630xexx991.htm). Inference from documents, not a company statement of a gap; preferred dividends (~$2.9m/qtr) 'can be suspended if needed' per the MD&A, which is a cash lever.

findings.finding: Q4 is set up to be the seasonal low: management guided Q4 cost of production in line with Q3 (~$110/lb), FY production ~1m lbs implies Q4 ~285k lbs (152k+246k+317k = 715k through Q3), below Q3's 317k; Q4 2025 ASP was $146 vs $155 in Q3 2025; California outdoor wholesale was $334/lb in the week of Sep 25 with a 13-22m lb wet October harvest projected. Q4 gross margin at or below Q3's 26% and lower revenue than Q3 is the likely shape of any Q4 commentary; the original FY guide (ASP mid-$180s, revenue $235-245m) is out of reach with YTD ASP ~$176 and YTD revenue ~$144m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Pricing disappointment drove the Oct 19 prelim reaction: -22.88% on 16.2m shares when Q3 ASP came in at $150 vs $211 in Q2. The Q2 print (Aug 13) moved -5.62% then +2.98% the next day (baseline history; these two and Oct 19 are the only confirmed results events in it).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the prelim already flagged 'challenging California market pricing'. What is not yet public is a Q4 ASP or revenue number, or a formal reset of the FY revenue/ASP guide; if the market were pricing a Q4 bounce the stock would not have made new lows after the Oct 26 reiteration.
findings.independence: Q4 cost and production guide: Oct 26 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000110465926118806/tm2628296d1_ex99-1.htm). Q4 2025 ASP $146: Q4 2025 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000184873126000013/ghbi2025q46-kerex991.htm). Industry price series is a proxy (Cannabis Benchmarks via Cannabis Business Times, https://www.cannabisbusinesstimes.com/top-stories/news/15836802/california-harvest-preview-a-complex-croptober-meets-soft-prices, snippet only, page 403).

findings.finding: Stale EPS consensus will print as a miss: listed consensus is EPS $0.01-0.02, but with Q3 gross profit $14.9m (pre-released) against Q2 total operating expenses of $18.8m and preferred distributions of ~$2.9m a quarter, the quarter implies an operating loss of roughly $4m and a net loss to common; revenue ($56.8m) beats the $52-56m estimates, already public.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2: FXEmpire records an EPS beat and revenue miss; the stock moved -5.62% then +2.98% (baseline). No clean EPS-surprise history for this name.
findings.why_not_priced: Headline screens will show an EPS miss against a $0.01 consensus that predates the prelim; most holders already know the gross profit, so the effect is optics on headline-reading flow, capped small because the bar is disputed across three sources.
findings.independence: Consensus: Chartmill https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/GLAS/estimates and Benzinga https://kr.benzinga.com/quote/GLAS/earnings-forecasts (both snippets, disagree on revenue). Gross profit: Oct 19 prelim (https://finviz.com/news/403857/glass-house-brands-reports-preliminary-unaudited-third-quarter-financial-results-and-resignation-of-john-nichols-jr-from-board-of-directors).

findings.finding: Possible first 2027 frame: in the Q2 release management guided a year-end 2026 production run rate above 1.1m lbs with Greenhouse 2 fully contributing, and the Oct prelim reiterated the $95/lb long-term cost target (Q3 actual $110); a 2027 volume/cost outlook on tonight's call would be the first forward number since the FY guide went stale, and at 1.1m lbs x ~$150 the biomass revenue run rate is ~$165m against a ~$110m equity value.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Oct 26 reiteration of the 1m lb FY forecast and $95 target (with ATM off) was followed by +9.35% on Oct 27; the Q2 release's run-rate guide coincided with -5.62% (baseline, stockanalysis). The name has mostly sold its positives since September.
findings.why_not_priced: No 2027 guide exists yet, so any number given is new; at $1.17 the market is pricing either a much lower price per pound or dilution, so a credible volume and cost frame funded from existing cash would be visibly different from the current price. Shrunk because this name has sold good news and cost targets have slipped before (Q1 cost $175 vs a ~$100 target).
findings.independence: Oct 26 6-K reiteration of the $95 target and 1m lbs (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1848731/000110465926118806/tm2628296d1_ex99-1.htm); shares ~89m at June 30 plus ~4m from the Q3 ATM and warrants (Q2 release and Oct prelim).

lessons_applied: Lesson 4 (financing is a question): answered. The spend funds a corroborated ramp, but covenant pressure (FCCR breach at Dec 2025, test resumes Dec 31) and the $15m liquidity floor against ~$39m remaining spend keep it negative. The closing note (covenant arithmetic and inference lose to documents) shrank it from -2.5 to -1.5.
Lesson 6 (verify the bar): consensus disagrees across three sources, so the EPS-miss finding was capped from -0.5 to -0.3.

Lesson 1 and the untrustworthy-history note: the rebuilt confirmed-results reactions (Q2 -5.6/+3.0, prelim -22.9) and the sale of nearly every catalyst since September shrank the two positives: auditor relief from +1.5 to +1.0, 2027 frame from +1.0 to +0.7.
Lesson 5 (an unexplained drawdown is worth 0): positioning/oversold finding cut from +0.5 to +0.2. Kept on file per the core.
